title: Lesson 48 - Publishing and Maintaining Activations: Schedule, Monitoring, Consent, and Safe Deactivation
description: Publish Activations within Data 360, covering scheduling and publishing, monitoring success and failures, consent and governance at activation time, and deactivating safely.

questions.question: When is consent enforced for a Data 360 activation?
options: Only when the segment criteria are first saved
At activation time, using ingested and modeled consent preferences
Never, because consent is a CRM only concern
Only when the segment is a real-time segment
questions.explanation: Data 360 lets you ingest and model consent preferences, use them in segmentation, and check them at activation, so consent is enforced at activation time.

questions.question: An activation job reports success, but the marketing team sees no new audience. What is the most reliable next step?
options: Verify the destination object such as the data extension or file, and compare the activation count to the segment count
Change the segment type to dynamic
questions.explanation: A successful publish should be verified at the destination; a created data extension or file proves the pipeline end to end, and a large count gap points at contact point or consent filtering.

questions.question: What is the correct order when retiring an activation?
options: Delete the segment, then stop the activation
Pause or delete the activation, then handle the destination object, then adjust the segment schedule
Delete the destination object, then leave the activation running
Change the publish schedule to a real-time segment, then delete the target
questions.explanation: Stopping the activation first prevents further publishes, then the destination object is handled, and only then is the shared segment schedule adjusted, because other activations may rely on it.
